_about: The dashboard To-Do feed: a short, layman-readable daily checklist of curation work (for Sam) and engineering/pre-curation work (for Fable, the Claude session), rendered by cpl_todos.js as the 📋 To-Do button on every tab. Refreshed at every Rule-8 checkpoint alongside the session handoff (this file is the handoff distilled for the dashboard). Check-off state lives in each viewer's browser (localStorage) and resets when _as_of changes. Keep it SHORT — ≤ ~12 items; done items are deleted, not checked.
_as_of: 2026-08-12 (evening) · SkyLink — one college/district taxonomy, ready to write.
_status: Two things landed today. My College folded down around Sierra AI (SkyPro), and we finally assembled one college and district list: every spelling any of our systems uses — yours, MAP's and the Chancellor's Office's — tied to a single ID, with the district each college belongs to. 116 colleges, 73 districts, nothing unresolved. It is built but not yet switched on, because turning it on changes how every screen matches college names and needs two decisions from Sam first. Next session: making the Sierra Training tab something a person can triage from without technical vocabulary.

items.text: The My College tab now opens as Sierra AI plus nine closed sections, each showing one figure. Two things I'd like your eye on: do those one-line summaries on the closed rows earn their place, or would you rather the rows were bare? And should 'Start here' be the one section already open when the page loads?

Five colleges were being told they had no implementation funding at all — Mt. San Antonio, Norco, Reedley, MiraCosta and LA Southwest. A name-matching bug, now fixed; Mt. SAC correctly shows $522,239. Worth knowing in case anyone at those colleges saw the old page and drew a conclusion from it.

Three sections on My College are built and waiting for MAP links — adopt an exhibit, work student records, update contacts. You're checking with Malone and Pedro on the right URL shapes. Nothing else is blocked on this.

Still your call when you're ready: whether a college should be able to open its own page without signing in. It isn't a display change — four of the tab's figures are locked at the database, so opening it means deciding to publish student-derived totals and staff contacts.

Parked on your explanation: the two student counts on the tab disagree for most colleges because MAP records are being pulled for Exhibit correction and reloaded, so our copy is stale. Nothing to do until the MAP Custom Report fetch is on — we'll re-check then.

Wire the EACR prescriptive list into Supabase so Sierra can say which local course a college would most likely map a credential onto. Your catch, and it's now been open six sessions — the biggest piece of work nothing is blocking.

The project's always-loaded instruction file is half again as big as it should be, which taxes every session that starts. Move the long warning lists out of the two biggest roadmap entries into a reference doc and leave a pointer.

Twenty-five pieces of real feedback on Sierra are waiting to be read, eleven of them thumbs-down, the oldest sitting since 1 July. Measured live today — the automated test rows are excluded, and only four rows have ever been marked addressed.

Student-contact worklist, about ten minutes total: five colleges have a suggested counselling address nobody could verify (the network blocks their websites from here) — each needs about ten seconds in a browser to confirm; then fourteen colleges with no contact in MAP have a suggested one ready to send to the MAP team.

Two things here need a person, not a session: four colleges publish no usable address at all for a credit question, and the fifty-two colleges that do have a CPL Assistant were never checked for a student contact. Sessions are blocked from opening college websites, so this needs a human or a differently-connected runner.

Two things to ask the MAP team for, in one conversation: a feed of the CPL requests students submit (the one section of My College that cannot be built without it), and a durable row id for the student extract — the one we rely on today is an Access autonumber that renumbers on re-import.

Worth knowing before you talk to any college about their waiting credit: almost all of it is the same thing. Of the 64,074 units already articulated and waiting on a decision, 98.8% is credit for basic military service — mostly landing on a GE or graduation area rather than a named course. Sixty-five of the 73 colleges with any are at 100%. So it isn't hundreds of separate judgment calls, it's close to one decision applied over and over, for students who already have a DD-214 or JST on file. The page now says this. Thirty-three colleges have nothing waiting at all — that's a finished queue, not a gap.

A decision before we can finish the college-name cleanup. We now have one list that ties every spelling of every college — yours, MAP's, and the Chancellor's Office's — to a single ID, plus the district each belongs to. 116 colleges, 73 districts, nothing unresolved. Two questions: should districts get their own table, and should North Orange Continuing Education and San Diego College of Continuing Education be counted as colleges? Both have their own president but neither exists as a college in MAP, which may be why they show zero activity.

Sam's next priority: make this tab something he can actually triage from. Two separate problems — it isn't clear what to DO with a piece of feedback or when you're finished with it, and it's written in build-team language. Start by triaging one real row end to end and writing down where you stall; that list is the spec. 25 rows are waiting, 11 of them thumbs-down.
